clue.text: In general, intelligence can crack part of sentence that's unknown

indicators.note: to crack something is to break into it, so the intelligence word goes into the middle of the others

parts.note: a clause is a part of a sentence with its own verb
Z is one of the letters mathematicians use for an unknown quantity
wit is quick intelligence

explanation.surface: Broadly speaking, cleverness can unlock the mystery bit of a sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In general' reads as 'generally', but the definition is a military general, the Prussian theorist; 'In' merely links.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl von Clausewitz was a Prussian general and author of the military treatise On War.

clue.text: Man needs constant praise

parts.note: c is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
to laud is to praise

explanation.surface: A fellow who needs to be complimented all the time.
explanation.definitionFit: Claud is a man's first name, so it can stand for a man in crosswords.

clue.text: Spray into a crop when shooting stops

indicators.note: the spray goes into the other pieces

parts.note: rice is a cereal crop
mist is a fine spray

explanation.surface: Crop-spraying resumes on the farm once the gunfire has ceased.
explanation.definitionFit: An armistice is a truce, the point at which fighting in a war ceases.

clue.text: It's worth giving up saving

parts.note: the sum an insurer pays if you cash in a savings policy early

explanation.definitionFit: This is the cash sum paid out when a life insurance or savings policy is cashed in early.

clue.text: Stroll to court, and leave angrily

definitions.meaning: to go out walking with a sweetheart, an old way of courting

explanation.definitionFit: Couples once courted by strolling out together; and departing in protest is the other meaning.

clue.text: Dog biting one damaged part of leg

indicators.note: biting means the outer word closes around the other

parts.note: to dog someone is to tail or follow them

indicators.note: damaged means the letters are knocked into a different order

explanation.surface: A dog bites someone, injuring their leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog' looks like the animal but is the verb: TAIL. 'damaged' turns ONE into OEN, which goes after the T.
explanation.definitionFit: The nail on the toe sits at the very end of the leg, broadly understood.

clue.text: 7's predecessor's short drink

indicators.note: short means cut off before its end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: the answer to 7 down is the month April, and the month before it is March

explanation.surface: A brief tipple taken by the person who came before someone else.
explanation.definitionFit: Marc is a brandy distilled from the leftover skins and pips of pressed grapes.

clue.text: Some days, picked up a penny in foreign money

indicators.note: the penny goes inside the currency
picked up, in a down clue, means read upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: the lira was the currency of Italy and is still used in Turkey

explanation.surface: Collecting a coin in a foreign currency on certain days.
explanation.definitionFit: April is a month of thirty days, so it is some days of the year.

clue.text: Mark pausing saves a single run this time

indicators.note: to save something is to keep it inside, so the other pieces go within

parts.note: a comma is a punctuation mark showing a pause
a single is one
r is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A cricketer, Mark, hesitating, prevents a single run being taken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a batsman's name; it is a punctuation mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The Common Era is the present era of dating, the current period of time.

clue.text: Having healthy heart, like a lamb

definitions.meaning: with no heart murmur, a sign of a sound heart

explanation.definitionFit: A heart without a murmur is healthy; doing something meekly without complaint is the idiom.

clue.text: Dim possibilities in vanishing sea, for him?

definitions.text: Dim possibilities in vanishing sea, for him?

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go inside the name of the sea

parts.note: the Aral Sea in Central Asia has largely dried up and is a famous vanishing sea

indicators.note: the possibilities of a word are its other arrangements, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A naval officer gloomily contemplating a sea that is drying up beneath him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibilities' shuffles DIM to DMI, which 'in' places inside ARAL; the whole clue then describes the sort of person for whom the sea matters.
explanation.definitionFit: An admiral is a senior naval commander, someone whose career depends on the sea.

clue.text: Stuff to say, with constant interruption, that's quotable

definitions.note: read as a noun phrase: something that's quotable

indicators.note: an interruption breaks in, so the constant cuts into the word for say

parts.note: e.g. (for example) is a common abbreviation for say
pi is the mathematical constant
to ram is to stuff or cram

explanation.surface: Advice on what to say, interrupted repeatedly, that nonetheless proves memorable.
explanation.definitionFit: An epigram is a short witty saying, the kind of remark people love to repeat.

clue.text: Fails to exorcise one devil, a wronged wife

indicators.note: exorcising drives something out, so a letter is removed

parts.note: an engine dies when it fails
I is the Roman numeral for one
a demon is a devil

explanation.surface: Attempts to drive out a demon go wrong, and a mistreated wife suffers.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'a wronged wife', not just 'wife', so the A at the end is part of the wordplay, not the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Desdemona is Othello's wife in Shakespeare, falsely accused of adultery and killed.

clue.text: I say room's round

parts.note: a hall is a large room; the 's is just a link meaning has
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A remark that the room is circular.
explanation.definitionFit: Hallo is an exclamation of greeting or surprise, much like crying out a mild exclamation.

clue.text: Regularly went quiet, then told stories

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
telling stories is a mild way of saying someone fibbed

explanation.surface: Someone who habitually went silent and then made things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' looks like an alternate-letter instruction, but here it belongs to the definition: a ferry plies a route by travelling it regularly.
explanation.definitionFit: To ply a route is to travel it regularly, as a ferry or bus does.

clue.text: Kiss you afterwards, said thief

indicators.note: said signals that the phrase is spoken and heard as one word

parts.note: a peck is a kiss, and afterwards is later: peck you later

explanation.surface: Someone promising a kiss later, who turns out to be a crook.
explanation.definitionFit: A peculator embezzles money entrusted to them, a kind of thief.

clue.text: Here martyrs reversed fate, before blood spilled?

indicators.note: before puts the turned word ahead of the next piece
reversed means the word is written backwards

parts.note: one's lot is one's fate
spilled blood forms a pool, a puddle

explanation.surface: A grim scene where martyrs turned their fortunes before a pool of blood.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tolpuddle Martyrs were Dorset farm labourers transported to Australia in 1834 for forming a trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dorset village of Tolpuddle gave its name to the martyrs, early trade unionists.

clue.text: Following group, clip sides in accident

indicators.note: being in an accident leaves things jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A car clips the sides of another in a crash.
explanation.definitionFit: Disciples are a band of followers of a teacher or leader.

clue.text: Beaten in trophy, leader stopped being miserable +

indicators.note: the scrambled letters sit inside the trophy word

parts.note: a cup is a sporting trophy

indicators.note: beaten means knocked about, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A team beaten in a cup match whose captain finally cheered up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beaten' turns LEADER into LEARED, which 'in' places inside CUP. The stray + in the source text is a printing mark, not part of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Weather that has cleared up has stopped being grey and gloomy; so too a person's mood.

clue.text: Holding pump in front, remove exhaust

indicators.note: holding means the outer word keeps the other piece inside it

parts.note: to delete is to remove

indicators.note: in front means only the leading letter is taken

explanation.surface: A mechanic holding a pump at the front of the car removes its exhaust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exhaust' looks like a car part, but it is the verb meaning use up.
explanation.definitionFit: To deplete is to use up or drain a supply, to exhaust it.

clue.text: Enquiry ending early disaster! —- with no charges

indicators.note: ending early means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a probe is an enquiry or investigation
O no! is a cry on seeing a disaster

explanation.surface: An inquiry is cut short in calamity, and nobody is charged.
explanation.definitionFit: Pro bono work is done for the public good, with no fee charged.

clue.text: Travelling, wanting two seats together? Not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely means the run is only partly used, losing letters from its ends
two calls for the word to be written out twice

parts.note: one seat each, written twice over

explanation.surface: A traveller hoping for a pair of seats side by side, but not quite getting them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'together' joins the two copies into SEATSEAT; 'Not entirely' trims SE from the front and T from the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at sea means being on a voyage, hence travelling by ship.

clue.text: Tadpole for one gets right inside rock

indicators.note: the rock gets the abbreviation put inside it
the rock gets the abbreviation put inside it

parts.note: lava is molten rock, and the rock it cools into

explanation.surface: A tadpole manages to wriggle inside a crevice in a rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A tadpole is the larval form of a frog or toad, an example of a larva.

clue.text: Like mysterious characters in game to score shortly

parts.note: RU is rugby union, the game

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: to nick is to score a notch

explanation.surface: Strange figures in a match trying to score quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Runic letters are ancient Germanic script, often seen as mysterious symbols.

clue.text: Laying hands on wretch I point out?

indicators.note: the point goes out around the other pieces, i.e. outside them

parts.note: a prong is a sharp point, as on a fork
a cur is a contemptible wretch
a cur is a contemptible wretch

explanation.surface: A healer laying hands on some poor wretch and pointing out who it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point out' reads as a phrase meaning indicate, but 'out' is the container signal: CUR and I go inside PRONG.
explanation.definitionFit: Procuring means obtaining or acquiring, as in laying hands on something.

clue.text: Has to support Grand Theatre outfits

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece supports another by sitting beneath it

parts.note: G is short for grand, a thousand pounds
to own something is to have it

explanation.surface: A grand theatre has to finance its costumes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grand Theatre' reads as a venue's name; the theatre is an operating theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgeons wear gowns in the operating theatre.

clue.text: Bald bit —- uncertain if part is to be put back

indicators.text: part is to be put back
indicators.note: only part of the word for uncertain is put back, i.e. turned round

parts.note: uncertain is not sure; its first word is the part turned around
the second half of not sure

explanation.surface: A balding patch, of uncertain origin, which may need some hair put back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncertain' gives NOT SURE; 'part is to be put back' reverses only NOT to TON, leaving SURE alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonsure is the shaved patch on a monk's head, a deliberately bald area.

clue.text: Current rule how alms are to be distributed

indicators.note: letters to be distributed are dealt out in a new order

explanation.surface: Today's regulation on how charitable donations should be handed out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like 'present-day', but it means electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: Ohm's law relates electric current, voltage and resistance in a circuit, a basic physical law.

clue.text: Place of torture associated with ruin

definitions.meaning: a frame on which victims were stretched
the phrase ... and ruin means decay and destruction

explanation.definitionFit: The rack was a torture frame, and the idiom rack and ruin pairs the word with ruin.

clue.text: Pleasant situation in tea garden?

parts.note: a comfortable easy life, and literally a flower plot of tea roses in a garden

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means an easy comfortable situation; a garden of tea roses would literally contain one.
